steps.body: Jumps come in sizes: tens devour distance, ones finish the job. A good plan spends big jumps first and small jumps last.
steps.narration: Jumps come in sizes: tens devour distance, ones finish the job. A good plan spends big jumps first and small jumps last.

widget.prompt: Cover the tens of a 32-journey: three ten-hops from 40.

commonLandings.feedback: Three ones cover 3 of the 32 — the big jumps belong first.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10, going forward. From 40, 3 hops land on 70.
widget.successFeedback: 70 — the tens are spent; two little one-jumps would finish at 72.

predict.prompt: To travel 32 along the line, which plan wins?
predict.reveal: Both arrive, but the mixed plan takes five jumps where ones-only takes thirty-two.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2l jump sizes.
invariants: Position on the line IS the number: equal jumps cover equal amounts, and a journey's landing depends only on start, jump size, and direction for g2l jump sizes.
misconceptions: Treating marks as decoration — unequal spacing, jumps of the wrong size, or reading a start mark as a landing.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which change — start, jump size, or direction — would move the landing, and which would leave it alone?

widget.prompt: From 40 to 72: which jump plan is fastest to run?

options.label: Three ten-jumps, then two one-jumps
options.feedback: Correct — big jumps cover the tens (30) and small jumps finish the ones (2): five jumps total.

options.label: Thirty-two one-jumps
options.feedback: Thirty-two tiny hops reach the same place at six times the effort — the line rewards big jumps first.

options.label: Four ten-jumps
options.feedback: Four tens overshoot to 80; a plan must land exactly, not merely nearby.

options.label: One giant jump of 100
options.feedback: A hundred-jump flies far past 72; jump sizes must fit the distance being covered.

hints: Jump the size the sum names.
